newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi cuts key rate to 35 from 45 pct from Sept 9.
newsitem.headline: Malawi cuts key rate to 35 from 45 pct from Sept 9.

text.p: Malawi's central bank said on Friday it was reducing its lending base rate by 10 percentage points to 35 percent from 45 percent, effective September 9.
Reserve Bank Governor Matthews Chikaonda told Reuters the move followed an improvement in economic fundamentals, including a sharply reduced budget deficit.
"Encouraged by the strength of the measures by government to control expenditure, the Reserve Bank of Malawi has found it necessary to review its policy stance," he said.
The Bank's base lending rate was last cut in June to 45 percent from 50 percent.
Chikaonda added that some commercial banks had already reduced their lending rates to 36 percent.

Malawi's annual inflation rate has fallen from 98.1 percent in July 1995 to 43.1 percent in July 1996, while the 1995/96 budget deficit has been reduced to 5.5 percent of GDP from 14.9 percent in 1994/95.
Foreign reserves have risen to over US$100 million, representing five months import cover, compared to four months a year ago.
Chikaonda said the improvements were in line with International Monetary Fund/World Bank targets.
